newsitem.title: INDIA: India targets 7 pct GDP growth/yr over 10 yrs - PM.
newsitem.headline: India targets 7 pct GDP growth/yr over 10 yrs - PM.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda said on Tuesday his government was committed to achieving seven percent annual growth of gross domestic product (GDP) over the next 10 years.
"India is committed to achieving GDP growth of seven percent over the next 10 years, and 12 percent growth in industrial production," Deve Gowda told a conference on foreign investment in India.
The targets were in line with long-term economic objectives which Deve Gowda's government set after taking office in June.
Deve Gowda said the objectives would be achieved with low fiscal deficits and low inflation.
The prime minister also said that India aimed for capital formation of 30 percent of GDP, which would be higher than the domestic savings rate of 24 percent.
"Future refinements are on the way to make it (India) investment friendly," he said.
Heavy inflows of foreign investment are central to the government's economic liberalisation drive.
